title: The Provision of Cape Reckoning
premise: Isandro Fairweather, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a disaster he refuses to explain, has spent two decades leading quiet expeditions and keeping his past at arm's length. When his old rival Marisol Vega hires his crew for an impossible job—following the Río Ceniza upstream to its forbidden source before the dry season ends—he realizes she knows what happened twenty years ago, and that the source hides something belonging to him: his father's lost survey records, proof of who he really is. As the river narrows and old betrayals surface among the crew, Isandro must choose between staying invisible and claiming a legacy that could destroy or redeem him. In the end, he reaches the source, confronts Marisol's truth about the original disaster, and chooses to return downstream—not to erase his past, but to finally belong to the people waiting for him there.
about_author: Paloma Almeida is a former river expedition cook turned novelist who grew up between Portuguese fishing villages and Andean trailheads. She writes adventure stories about people who measure their lives in landscapes rather than calendars.

chapters.title: The Weight of Miles
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. On a routine high-altitude trek, Isandro measures his life in distances covered, avoiding letters from home and questions from his young crewmate Teo. When a courier delivers a contract bearing Marisol Vega's seal—the one job sworn off twenty years ago—his carefully mapped invisibility begins to crack. Emotional beat: restless denial.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Water
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Marisol arrives at the trailhead lodge with permits no blacklisted man should touch and a map of the Río Ceniza marked to its forbidden source. She offers double pay and a veiled threat: she knows what happened on the Cordillera Negra. Isandro refuses; his crew, hungry and loyal, quietly votes yes. Emotional beat: cornered pride.

chapters.title: The Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: POV Teo, the youngest guide. Teo observes the crew assembling—each member carrying a reason to be unfindable—and wonders why Isandro, their anchor, looks like a man being dragged. Preparations reveal Isandro's hidden fluency in the valley dialect, hinting at roots he denies. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into loyalty.

chapters.title: Downstream of Every Law
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The expedition enters the Ceniza gorge, where maps fail and checkpoints are bribed. Marisol travels with them, trading barbs with Isandro that carry twenty years of unfinished argument. A rockslide nearly kills Teo; Isandro's split-second rescue reveals skills he claims not to have. Emotional beat: the past pressing closer.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Through her eyes we learn fragments: twenty years ago, Isandro's father led a survey into these headlands and never returned, and Isandro took the blame for the expedition's collapse. Marisol isn't hunting treasure—she's hunting the truth her own family buried. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: The Dry Season's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Water grows scarce as they climb; the crew rations hope along with the last canteens. A rival outfit, hired by someone inside Marisol's company, shadows them through the canyons. Teo catches Isandro burning a letter from home and confronts him—belonging, Teo argues, isn't a place you flee. Emotional beat: fracture within the found family.

chapters.title: Blacklist Country
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Ambushed at a narrow ford, the crew loses supplies and Marisol is injured. Isandro confesses the truth of the Cordillera Negra: he abandoned the survey to save a drowning boy, and the disaster that followed was blamed on him by men who needed a scapegoat. Emotional beat: confession as release.

chapters.title: The Source of All Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Climbing past the last waterfall, Isandro finds the hidden survey camp and his father's records—including evidence that Marisol's family caused the original betrayal. Marisol, arriving wounded but determined, must decide whether to let the truth out. Above them, the dry season's final heat cracks the glacier feed. Emotional beat: reckoning at the roof of the world.

chapters.title: Upstream of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. With the rival outfit closing in, Marisol chooses truth over inheritance: she broadcasts the records' contents, destroying her family's claim and clearing Isandro's name. The descent becomes a race against the dying river, the crew pulling together as the water they followed vanishes behind them. Emotional beat: sacrifice and solidarity.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the river's mouth, Isandro opens the letter he once burned—an invitation from the sister he left behind—and answers it. No longer measuring life in miles, he plans a season of guiding with Teo at his side, his name restored and his belonging claimed. Emotional beat: arrival, at last, in his own life.
